metadata.title: PIRLS 2021 in Northern Ireland: Reading Attainment

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report uses PIRLS 2021 sampling and scaling procedures to produce nationally representative estimates for Northern Ireland, based on a sample of 143 schools and 4050 pupils. The report states that Northern Ireland met international sampling requirements once replacement schools were included, and it reports participation rates (weighted) and uncertainty via standard errors. However, the manuscript does not name specific PIRLS weight variables (e.g., student design weights) or replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For analysts using PIRLS microdata, the appropriate approach is to apply the PIRLS complex survey weights and replicate design (as provided in the international database) when estimating means, benchmark proportions, and subgroup differences, and to use the PIRLS scaling/benchmarking outputs to ensure comparability across paper/digital modes.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report is a descriptive national PIRLS report summarising attainment, distributions, and contextual questionnaire results; it does not present an ML model that requires explicit plausible-value (PV) handling choices for a cognitive achievement target. PIRLS achievement is reported using PIRLS international scaling and benchmark procedures rather than an author-trained predictive model with documented PV pooling rules. Missing-data handling is therefore not described at the level of an ML estimation pipeline in the provided text, which is a reporting gap for any attempt to reproduce PV-based estimates from microdata.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PIRLS 2021 Northern Ireland national sample: 143 schools and 4050 pupils participated (Year 6 in Northern Ireland internationally Grade 4; due to COVID-19 delay, pupils were at the start of Year 7/internationally Grade 5). The report notes that replacement schools were included to meet international sampling requirements; it also reports absence (456 pupils absent) and an overall exclusion rate of 5.5% (with pupil-level exclusions based on internationally agreed criteria). No further analytic subsample restrictions (e.g., specific item/module completion filters) are described in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This NFER report summarises PIRLS 2021 reading attainment for Northern Ireland, where pupils were assessed at the start of Year 7 (internationally Grade 5) due to COVID-19 delays. The report reports an average reading scale score of 566 for Northern Ireland, significantly above the PIRLS international centrepoint of 500, and provides cross-country comparisons with six comparator countries (Finland, Poland, Singapore, Republic of Ireland, Australia, England) while cautioning that delayed testing periods complicate interpretation. It also reports benchmark attainment: 23% reached the Advanced benchmark (625), 3% were below the Low benchmark (400), and it describes distributional spread using 10th/90th percentile scores (461 and 665; gap 204). Contextual chapters summarise gender differences (girls higher by 24 points), socio-economic gradients (FSME gap 49 points), and COVID-19 schooling experiences (e.g., 92% of pupils attended schools where >8 weeks of teaching were affected). The report is descriptive and does not implement or evaluate machine-learning predictive models.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The provided text is a descriptive large-scale assessment report (attainment, benchmarks, and contextual questionnaire distributions) rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. As a result, there is no ML target variable, no model training/evaluation, and no documented PV pooling or missing-data strategy for an ML pipeline. The extraction therefore leaves ML-specific fields empty and focuses on assessment design and reported PIRLS outcomes.
